## Overview

Offline embedding refresh is an operational pattern for managing vector embeddings in search and retrieval systems. It is a scheduled batch process that regenerates embeddings for a corpus (full or incremental) when either:

- The underlying embedding model changes (upgrade, retrain, or swap to a new model)
- Source documents update in bulk (content refresh, corpus expansion)

Rather than updating embeddings on-demand or incrementally per document, offline refresh runs on a fixed cadence and atomically swaps new vectors into the retrieval index. This avoids serving mixed-model results during the transition.

## Operational Concerns

### Model Versioning
Each batch of embeddings should be versioned alongside the embedding model used to generate them. This enables tracking which model produced which vectors, supports rollback to prior embeddings, and aids in debugging quality regressions.

### Vector Drift Monitoring
When swapping embedding models, the new vectors will differ geometrically from the old ones. Monitoring drift — measuring the statistical divergence between old and new embeddings — helps detect unexpected or problematic shifts in semantic representation before they impact retrieval quality.

### Blue/Green Index Staging
A blue/green deployment pattern for the retrieval index allows the new embeddings to be staged and tested against live traffic (or in shadow mode) before becoming the default. If quality regressions occur, the system can roll back to the previous (blue) index without customer impact. The swap is typically atomic.

- **[[vector-index]]** — the data structure serving embeddings to retrieval queries
- **[[rag-pattern]]** — the broader pattern in which offline refresh often operates (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
